facts.text: On this date in 1775, the United States Marine Corps was founded in a Philadelphia tavern — Tun Tavern, which was also a brewery.
On Nov 10, 1989, the first checkpoint in the Berlin Wall opened at Bornholmer Street, one day after the Wall 'fell' — most people don't know the two events were separate.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than live in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.
Indonesia spans a wider longitude than the continental United States, yet it has only three time zones — a political choice to keep the nation feeling unified.
The city of Istanbul straddles two continents, but fewer than 3% of its 15 million residents actually live on the Asian side.
On this date in 1923, Germany's hyperinflation peaked so severely that a single US dollar bought 4.2 trillion marks. Workers were paid twice daily so they could spend wages before they lost value.
On Nov 10, 1483, Martin Luther was born — the man whose 95 Theses inadvertently turbocharged European capitalism by sanctifying thrift, labor, and the rejection of indulgences as a financial product.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded in 1792 under a buttonwood tree with 24 brokers and a fixed commission of 0.25%. That cartel on commissions survived, largely intact, for 183 years.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion — the largest in history. It valued the company at $1.7 trillion, briefly making it worth more than the entire German stock market.
The S&P 500 has historically risen more in the six months after a US presidential election than in any other equivalent window — regardless of which party wins.

On this date in 1970, the Soviet Lunokhod 1 became the first remote-controlled robot to rove another world. It outlasted its planned 3-month mission by nearly a year, driven by a crew in Moscow like a very slow, lunar car.
On this date in 1983, Microsoft Word was released — but its first users ran it on MS-DOS and had to use a mouse, a device so unfamiliar that Microsoft bundled a live demo mouse with the software.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces most of its atoms every few years, yet the pattern that makes you recognizably you persists. You are less a thing than a process — a wave, not a particle.
Mantis shrimp see the world through 16 types of color receptors. Humans have 3. They do not see more colors so much as they process color in an entirely different, still poorly understood way.
On this day in 1775, the U.S. Marines were founded — in a bar. Samuel Nicholas recruited the first troops at Tun Tavern in Philadelphia.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, twenty-one years before anyone could send a message by telephone.
On this day in 1444, the Ottoman army crushed a Christian crusade at Varna — the last serious attempt by Europe to reclaim Constantinople, nine years before it fell for good.
Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire by roughly 250 years. It was teaching students before Tenochtitlán was even a plan.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramids were already ancient history to her.
Today in 1871, Stanley found Livingstone — but the famous greeting he used, 'I presume,' is classic British understatement: 'presume' traces to Latin *praesumere*, to take for granted before knowing.
Today in 1969, Sesame Street premiered — 'sesame' comes from Arabic *simsim*, itself from ancient Akkadian *šamaššammū*, making this humble seed one of the oldest named plants in human language.
The Finnish word *myötähäpeä* means the shame you feel on someone else's behalf — a vicarious cringe with no single-word equivalent in English, though the feeling is universal.
The English word 'glamour' is a corruption of 'grammar.' In medieval Scotland, grammar meant arcane learning, which slid into 'gramarye' (magic), then 'glamour' — a spell cast over the eyes.

The Portuguese word *saudade* describes a longing for something you may never have had — its earliest documented use dates to the 13th century, and linguists still argue whether it is fully translatable.
On this date in 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had burned over 1 million ETH in its first 90 days — permanently removing more supply than miners were creating, flipping ETH briefly deflationary.
On Nov 10, 2022, FTX halted withdrawals. Within 72 hours, an $8B hole was confirmed, making it the fastest collapse of a top-5 exchange in crypto history.
Bitcoin's timechain has never once produced blocks at exactly its 10-minute target. The actual median inter-block time since genesis is closer to 9.5 minutes, because the difficulty algorithm lags.

The DAO hack of 2016 wasn't a smart contract bug — it was a logic flaw. The attacker drained 3.6M ETH by calling a withdrawal function recursively before balances updated, a pattern now called reentrancy.

Satoshi's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not just a timestamp. It's a direct editorial on why Bitcoin existed, embedded permanently on-chain.

On this date in 2016, Microsoft announced a 95.9% word error rate on the Switchboard speech recognition benchmark—matching human performance for the first time, a milestone researchers had expected would take another decade.
On this date in 2022, Meta released Galactica, a 120B-parameter science LLM. It was pulled after 72 hours when users demonstrated it confidently fabricated citations, dosages, and historical facts.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity—comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, for a single training pass.

The first neural network to defeat a professional Go player, AlphaGo, learned primarily from 30 million human moves—then its successor AlphaGo Zero surpassed it using zero human game data, trained entirely through self-play.

Transformer attention scales quadratically with sequence length: doubling the context window quadruples the compute cost of each forward pass, which is why extending context from 4K to 1M tokens required fundamental architectural changes.
